subject: Deployment-mode decision and Dedicated sizing scenario playbook
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@curahealth.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@curahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — deployment mode tradeoffs + dedicated sizing scenario playbook

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great to speak earlier. Below is a concise post-call recap and the proposed next steps so we converge on whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private VPC is the best fit for CuraHealth. I attached a short capacity workbook so you can drop in traffic samples.

Recap of requirements you shared:
- Workload: conversational triage + structured document summarization for patient intake. Mix: ~70% short chat (avg 40 tokens), 25% mid-length (100–300 tokens), 5% long-form summarization (400–900 tokens).
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 120ms for chat; allowed up to 600ms for longer summarization calls.
- TPS targets: baseline 150 TPS (concurrent users), peak 450 TPS during business hours; expected growth 20% q/q.
- Security: PHI in payloads — must be in-scope for SOC2 / customer-managed KMS if we go Private.
- Preference: want Redwood Dedicated if we can meet latency and cost goals; open to Hosted for initial POC.

Questions / clarifications we need to size Dedicated:
1) Token mix confirmation: do you expect the 5% long-form to average ~700 tokens when triggered?
2) Concurrency model: is a single user session expected to generate multiple back-to-back generation calls (i.e., streaming + function calls) or mostly single-shot messages?
3) Acceptable batching window: is 10–20ms acceptable for aggregating requests for cost-efficiency, or do you need cut-through at <5ms?

Candidate GPU types we should evaluate (tradeoffs):
- H100 (best for FP16/AMP and high throughput for long sequences; higher cost)
- A100 80GB (mature footprints, good for medium-length; competitive cost)
- L4 / T4x (cheaper, best for short-chat-heavy workloads but may struggle on long-form summarization).

Proposed next steps:
- You: drop 48 hours of representative request logs (timestamps, token counts, latencies) into the attached workbook.
- Redwood: Ben and I will produce a three-scenario sizing playbook (Conservative / Balanced / Cost-optimized) with recommended GPU mix, expected TPS per GPU, and estimated monthly committed throughput cost.
- Sync: 45-min follow-up next week to review the workbook output.

Attachments: cura_capacity_workbook.xlsx (workbook template), redwood_poc-metrics-spec.pdf (what we need in logs).

Thanks —
Tessa
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@curahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — deployment mode tradeoffs + dedicated sizing scenario playbook

Thanks, Tessa — solid recap. Quick answers inline:

1) Long-form: yes, when nurses upload visit notes we expect the summarization jobs to average ~650–800 tokens (~5% of traffic).
2) Concurrency: typical user session will produce 2–3 generation calls on average (initial triage + follow-up clarifying question), streaming enabled. High-frequency bursts happen when batch-insights jobs run at 03:00 AM but those are offline.
3) Batching window: we need chat latency to feel immediate — prefer cut-through <10ms, but a 15ms window is acceptable if it reduces costs materially.

Two other points:
- We prefer Dedicated for performance predictability and data isolation. Private VPC only if it helps meet KMS/audit requirements — otherwise Dedicated with isolated pools is fine.
- Budget: target committed spend for POC is $30k/month and roll to $70–100k/month if performance meets SLAs.

I'll upload a sanitized 72-hour sample to the workbook today. Can we surface a first-pass GPU-mix estimate before the follow-up? Even a back-of-envelope is helpful.

Cheers,
Alex
Head of Engineering | CuraHealth
alex.torres@curahealth.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@curahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-demo recap — quick ask for GPU-mix back-of-envelope

Ben / Karthik — forwarding Alex's answers (above). Alex is looking for a quick back-of-envelope GPU mix and expected TPS per GPU before our sync. Can you review and propose three scenarios (Conservative / Balanced / Cost-optimized) with these constraints:
- Baseline 150 TPS, peak 450 TPS; token mix as specified; 95th latency target <= 120ms for chat (avg 40 tokens).
- Allow 15ms batching for the cost-optimized scenario; Conservative must assume <5ms cut-through.
- Include hybrid mix possibilities (mix H100 + L4) and a fallback plan where we route long-form jobs to H100-backed pool to preserve chat latency.

Please paste the calculations in a reply so I can send a concise summary to Alex before the follow-up call.

Thanks —
Tessa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Torres <alex.torres@curahealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T11:24:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Re: Post-demo recap — quick ask for GPU-mix back-of-envelope

Thanks — did a quick back-of-envelope and pasted scenario summaries below. Caveats: these are round numbers for capacity planning; we'll run the workbook through our perf model for tighter numbers after we ingest the trace.

Assumptions used:
- Short chat (40 tokens) avg generation time: ~12ms on L4 (batched), ~6ms on A100, ~4ms on H100 (streaming cut-through differences).
- Mid-length (150 tokens) avg generation time: ~45ms L4, ~24ms A100, ~16ms H100.
- Long-form (700 tokens) avg generation time: ~320ms A100, ~210ms H100 (batch-friendly).
- Effective concurrency per GPU: estimate 1) L4: 10–18 concurrent short-chat streams (with batching); 2) A100: 25–40; 3) H100: 35–60 (model dependent).

Scenarios (Target: support peak 450 TPS with buffer):
1) Conservative (low latency, <5ms cut-through):
   - GPU choice: 100% H100 pool
   - Effective peak tokens/sec workload: approx 450 TPS * avg 60 tokens/request ~= 27k tokens/sec
   - H100 throughput (mixed): assume 800–1,200 tokens/sec per GPU (conservative) -> ~23–34 H100s -> Recommend 36 H100s for headroom and redundancy.
   - Estimated monthly committed cost (ballpark): $160k–$200k (depends on region/commit terms).

2) Balanced (latency-sensitive but cost-aware, 10–15ms batching):
   - GPU choice: hybrid H100 (long-form) + A100 (chat/mid) with small L4 pool for strictly short bursts.
   - Example mix: 8 H100s (handle long-form & overflow), 18 A100s (steady chat and mid-length), 6 L4s (cheap burst handling).
   - Rationale: route long summarisations to H100s to keep chat pools responsive; A100s give good cost/perf for mid-length.
   - Estimated monthly committed cost: $80k–$110k.

3) Cost-optimized (15ms batching, aggressive KV/prefix caching):
   - GPU choice: primarily A100 + L4s; H100s only as scheduled workers for nightly/large jobs.
   - Example mix: 6 H100 (scheduled long jobs), 12 A100, 12 L4 -> use dynamic routing and caching to keep chat latency near target.
   - Estimated monthly committed cost: $45k–$65k.

Operational notes:
- KV / prefix caching will shrink effective token throughput needs for chat (if same users re-query), so be sure to instrument cache-hit rates in the POC traces.
- Autoscaling / burst policies should be configured to fail open to Hosted-compatible pools for short interruptions (we can propose an SLA-safe fallback).

Next step: once you drop the logs in the workbook, we will run the Redwood perf model and return a 1-page sizing playbook with explicit per-GPU throughput numbers, estimated p95 latency curves, and committed spend ranges.

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
